newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: APEC economies differ on market opening pace - ADB.
newsitem.headline: APEC economies differ on market opening pace - ADB.

text.p: APEC economies have decided to set their own pace in liberalising their domestic capital markets, a senior Asian Development Bank (ADB) official said on Friday.

Paul Dickie, ADB director for Infrastructure, Energy & Financial Sectors Department, said many East Asian economies were still wary over the unrestricted flow of private capital coming on the heels of bad experiences in Latin America and some Asian economies.

"Some of the East Asian economies felt it very important that they have what you will call the deepening of the financial sector first, before they open up to freer movement of capital," Dickie said at a news conference. He did not mention which economies.
"They want to make sure that the domestic financial system is fully responsive to market changes and is soundly based...before they open the capital account," he added.
Finance ministers from the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum's 18 members are meeting in Cebu this weekend to discuss liberalising capital markets and other topics.
New Zealand has been pushing for a freer flow of funds within the Asia-Pacific region. The United States is reported to be strongly supporting the effort.
Dickie has been appointed to help APEC finance officials develop financial and capital markets in order to draw private funds to finance capital-intensive infrastructure projects.
Only 10 percent of the infrastructure financing in Asia comes from the private sector. Most was being shouldered by governments and multilateral financing institutions, he said.
The ADB has been pushing for the development of domestic bond markets in order to address the long-term financing requirements of large infrastructure projects.
Dickie said deputy finance ministers from the member economies were willing to compromise in order to achieve a consensus. The deputy ministers met on Friday.

Among the basic principles they have achieved were to provide a sound macroeconomic environment, a stable and transparent legal and regulatory system, sectoral policies that promote competition and availability of long term capital.
"They are just enunciating these principles and saying that they are desirable objectives... It is not going beyond those kinds of statement," he said.
According to the ADB, APEC economies need $1.5 trillion in the next decade to finance infrastructure.

APEC groups Australia, Brunei, Canada, Chile, China, Hong Kong, Indonesia, Japan, South Korea, Malaysia, Mexico, New Zealand, Papua New Guinea, the Philippines, Singapore, Taiwan, Thailand and the United States.
